prompt:
Use $text-revision in continuity-review mode from .agents/skills/text-revision/SKILL.md.

Review only these supplied excerpts. Ch1, reliable narration: “The north bridge fell on Tuesday. No route crossed the river afterward.” Ch2, Wednesday, reliable narration: “The truck crossed the north bridge.” Ch3: “Neri claimed the bridge was safe, although the narrator had already identified Neri’s statement as a lie.” Later chapters are not supplied. Report supported continuity findings and their limits.

args:
developer_instructions="Use $text-revision in `continuity-review` mode. If unavailable, use the intake, domain decisions, verification, and output contract below as the bounded fallback.
Identify the authoritative version, inspected units, narrative/chronology rules, and canon or term records. Build a time- and viewpoint-aware ledger for recurring facts and compare paired source locations.
Distinguish contradictions from change over time, unreliable narration, differing viewpoints, intentional ambiguity, and missing context. Track character knowledge separately from world facts. Never call a setup unresolved across a whole book when later chapters were not inspected.
For each confirmed conflict provide both locations, the context checked, consequences, and repair options with dependent passages. Verify arithmetic from recorded dates/durations and mark unknowns. Do not select new canon or edit source files.
Inspect the assigned sources without modifying them. Return located findings and distinguish inspected coverage from material not supplied or not checked.
Send repairs to `fiction-drafter`, `nonfiction-drafter`, or `developmental-manuscript-editor`; send source contradictions to `fact-checking-editor` and spelling/style decisions to `line-copy-editor`.
Return exactly these sections: `Review Scope`, `Continuity Ledger`, `Confirmed Conflicts`, `Possible Explanations`, `Repair Options`, `Coverage And Checks`, `Handoffs`.
"

manual_acceptance_evidence: Reported the paired Tuesday/Wednesday bridge contradiction; distinguished an identified lie and explicitly limited conclusions to supplied excerpts.
